# files

Filesystem chores: disk usage, directory creation, locating things on disk, and reclaiming space from node_modules trees.

---

## `files_disk_usage`

Print the size of each given path, human readable, smallest first. With no arguments it measures every entry in the current directory, dotfiles included, without ever walking up into the parent.

**Usage**

```sh
files_disk_usage [path]...
```

**Examples**

```sh
files_disk_usage
files_disk_usage ~/Downloads ~/Movies
```

**OS** any &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/common/files.sh:15`](../../modules/common/files.sh#L15)

**See also** `path_size`

---

## `files_find_node_modules`

List every node_modules directory below the current directory with its size, largest last. The result is cached per directory because the scan is slow; pass --refresh to rescan.

**Usage**

```sh
files_find_node_modules [--refresh]
```

**Examples**

```sh
files_find_node_modules
files_find_node_modules --refresh
```

**OS** any &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/common/files.sh:98`](../../modules/common/files.sh#L98)

---

## `files_list_command_path`

Long-list every real file a command name resolves to on PATH, so you can see symlinks, permissions and shim wrappers at a glance.

**Usage**

```sh
files_list_command_path <command>
```

**Examples**

```sh
files_list_command_path python3
```

**OS** any &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/common/files.sh:55`](../../modules/common/files.sh#L55)

## `files_locate_function`

Print the file and line number where a shell function was defined. Works in both shells: zsh answers from `whence`, bash needs the extdebug option toggled around `declare -F`.

**Usage**

```sh
files_locate_function <function-name>
```

**Examples**

```sh
files_locate_function files_mkcd
```

**OS** any &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/common/files.sh:74`](../../modules/common/files.sh#L74)

## `files_mkcd`

Create a directory (with parents) and change into it.

**Usage**

```sh
files_mkcd <directory>
```

**Examples**

```sh

```

## `files_mkdir_dated`

Create a timestamped directory and print its path. Useful for dump and capture directories that must not collide.

**Usage**

```sh
files_mkdir_dated [prefix]
```

**Examples**

```sh
files_mkdir_dated tcpdump
```

**OS** any &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/common/files.sh:41`](../../modules/common/files.sh#L41)

## `files_purge_node_modules`

Delete every node_modules directory below the current directory. Any arguments are treated as extended-regex patterns for paths to KEEP. Prints the full list and asks before removing anything.

> **⚠ DANGER** — Recursively deletes directories. Confirms once, then removes them all.

**Usage**

```sh
files_purge_node_modules [keep-pattern]...
```

**Examples**

```sh
files_purge_node_modules
files_purge_node_modules work/ important-project
```

**OS** any &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/common/files.sh:133`](../../modules/common/files.sh#L133)

**See also** `files_find_node_modules`
